faqs.question: How long does company registration take?

faqs.question: What is the due date for filing company annual returns?
faqs.answer: AOC-4 (financial statements) is due within 30 days of AGM and MGT-7 (annual return) within 60 days of AGM. For most companies, AGM must be held within 6 months of the financial year end (i.e., by September 30).

faqs.question: What is TDS and when must it be deposited?
faqs.answer: TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) must be deposited by the 7th of the following month. TDS returns are quarterly — Q1 by July 31, Q2 by October 31, Q3 by January 31, and Q4 by May 31.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss the ROC filing deadline?
faqs.answer: Late ROC filings attract additional fees of ₹100 per day per form, with no upper cap. The company and its directors can also face disqualification. Early filing is always advisable.

faqs.question: Is a CA audit mandatory for all businesses?
faqs.answer: Tax audit under Section 44AB is mandatory for businesses with turnover above ₹1 crore (₹10 crore for digital transactions) and professionals with gross receipts above ₹50 lakh.

faqs.question: Can you handle compliance for multiple group companies?

faqs.question: Which company type is best for a startup?
faqs.answer: Private Limited Company is generally recommended for startups planning to raise investment. LLP works well for professional service firms with two or more partners.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital required to register a company?
faqs.answer: There is no minimum paid-up capital requirement for Private Limited or LLP registration in India since 2015. You can start with any amount.

faqs.question: Can NRIs or foreign nationals be directors?
faqs.answer: Yes. At least one director must be a resident Indian (stayed 182+ days in the previous year). Foreign nationals and NRIs can be additional directors.

faqs.question: How many people are needed to register a Private Limited Company?
faqs.answer: A minimum of 2 directors and 2 shareholders are required. These can be the same individuals.

faqs.question: Is GST registration required after company registration?
faqs.answer: GST registration is mandatory when your turnover crosses the threshold (₹40L for goods, ₹20L for services) or when you do inter-state supplies.

faqs.question: Who qualifies for DPIIT Startup Recognition?
faqs.answer: Any entity incorporated in India (Private Limited, LLP, or Partnership) with less than 10 years of existence, annual turnover below ₹100 crore, and working on an innovative product/service/process.

faqs.question: Is DPIIT recognition free?

faqs.question: How long does the recognition last?
faqs.answer: DPIIT recognition is valid for the lifetime of the startup, as long as it meets the eligibility criteria (up to 10 years from incorporation or turnover below ₹100 crore).

faqs.question: What is the 80IAC tax exemption?
faqs.answer: Section 80IAC allows a DPIIT-recognised startup to claim 100% tax deduction on profits for any 3 consecutive years out of the first 10 years since incorporation, subject to IMB approval.

faqs.question: How long does 80IAC certification take?

faqs.question: When is GST registration mandatory?
faqs.answer: GST is mandatory when turnover exceeds ₹40 lakh (goods) or ₹20 lakh (services), for inter-state supply of any amount, for e-commerce sellers, and for reverse charge mechanism cases.

faqs.question: What is GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B?
faqs.answer: GSTR-1 reports outward supplies (sales invoices) and GSTR-3B is the monthly summary return with tax payment. Both are filed monthly (or quarterly for small taxpayers).

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late GST filing?
faqs.answer: Late fees of ₹50/day (₹20 for nil returns) per return, capped at ₹5,000 per return, plus 18% interest on outstanding tax.

faqs.question: Can I claim ITC on all business purchases?
faqs.answer: You can claim ITC on goods and services used for business purposes, subject to conditions. Certain items like food, personal use items, and some services are blocked credits.

faqs.question: What is a GST notice (DRC-01)?
faqs.answer: DRC-01 is a formal demand notice from the GST department for tax, interest, or penalty. It requires a written reply within the specified timeline — we handle this for you.

faqs.question: Is FSSAI licence mandatory for home-based food businesses?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any food business — including home kitchens — requires FSSAI registration if they sell food commercially. Basic registration applies if annual turnover is below ₹12 lakh.

faqs.question: How long does trademark registration take?
faqs.answer: Initial application acknowledgement is immediate. Full registration (trademark certificate) typically takes 18–24 months, but you can use ™ symbol from application date.

faqs.question: What is MSME/Udyam registration?
faqs.answer: Udyam is a free government registration for businesses classified as Micro, Small, or Medium based on investment and turnover. It gives access to priority lending, government schemes, and vendor preference.

faqs.question: Do I need IEC to sell on international e-commerce?
faqs.answer: Yes. Import Export Code (IEC) is mandatory for anyone importing goods into or exporting goods from India, including international online marketplace sellers.

faqs.question: What is the validity of FSSAI licence?
faqs.answer: FSSAI licences are valid for 1–5 years as chosen during application and must be renewed before expiry to avoid penalties.

faqs.question: Is Shop & Establishment registration required for offices?

faqs.question: What is the penalty for not registering under S&E?

faqs.question: What is the difference between 12A and 80G?

faqs.question: What is the last date to file ITR?
faqs.answer: For individuals and non-audit cases: July 31st. For tax audit cases: October 31st. For transfer pricing cases: November 30th. Belated returns can be filed by December 31st with penalty.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for not filing ITR?
faqs.answer: Late filing fee of ₹5,000 (₹1,000 if total income is below ₹5 lakh), plus 1% interest per month on unpaid tax under Section 234A.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to file ITR if TDS is already deducted?
faqs.answer: Yes. TDS deduction does not exempt you from ITR filing if your income exceeds the basic exemption limit. Filing also helps you claim refunds if excess TDS was deducted.

faqs.question: What is advance tax and when must it be paid?
faqs.answer: If your tax liability exceeds ₹10,000, you must pay advance tax in installments: 15% by June 15, 45% by September 15, 75% by December 15, and 100% by March 15.

faqs.question: Can I revise a filed ITR?
faqs.answer: Yes. A revised return can be filed anytime before December 31 of the relevant assessment year (or before assessment is complete, whichever is earlier).

faqs.question: What is the due date for company annual filing?

faqs.question: What happens if we don't file annual returns?
faqs.answer: Additional fees of ₹100 per day per form with no cap. If a company fails to file for 3 consecutive years, directors are disqualified under Section 164(2) and the company can be struck off.

faqs.question: Is INC-20A compulsory?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every company with share capital must file INC-20A (Declaration for Commencement of Business) within 180 days of incorporation, or the company cannot commence any business activity.

faqs.question: What is DIR-3 KYC and who must file it?
faqs.answer: DIR-3 KYC is an annual filing for every person who holds a Director Identification Number (DIN). It must be filed by September 30 each year to keep the DIN active.

faqs.question: Can we close a company that has no activity?
faqs.answer: Yes. A company with no liabilities or assets and no activity for 2 or more years can be struck off via STK-2 (Easy Exit Scheme). This is faster than formal winding up.

faqs.question: What is working capital?
faqs.answer: Working capital is the difference between current assets (inventory, debtors, cash) and current liabilities (creditors, short-term loans). Positive working capital means the business can meet its short-term obligations.

faqs.question: Why is cash flow more important than profit?
faqs.answer: A business can be profitable on paper but run out of cash if customers pay late, inventory is overstocked, or loans aren't managed. Cash flow determines day-to-day survival.

faqs.question: What is a 13-week cash flow forecast?
faqs.answer: A 13-week (3-month) rolling cash flow forecast shows weekly cash receipts and payments. It's a standard tool used by CFOs and lenders to manage near-term liquidity.

faqs.question: How do you improve debtor collections?
faqs.answer: We implement ageing reviews, payment reminder schedules, customer credit policies, and escalation procedures — systematically reducing your debtor days.

faqs.question: What is a cash conversion cycle?
faqs.answer: CCC = Debtor Days + Inventory Days − Creditor Days. A shorter CCC means cash comes in faster and goes out later — improving liquidity. We analyse and optimise your CCC.

faqs.question: What is a project report for a bank loan?
faqs.answer: A project report is a comprehensive document submitted to banks that covers the promoter's background, business description, market analysis, financial projections, repayment plan, and collateral details. It's mandatory for term loans.

faqs.question: What is CMA data?
faqs.answer: CMA (Credit Monitoring Arrangement) data is a standard format required by all banks for working capital assessment. It includes 3 years of historical financials, 2 years of projections, and key financial ratios.

faqs.question: What is Drawing Power (DP) in a cash credit account?
faqs.answer: Drawing Power is the maximum amount you can withdraw from your CC/OD account based on the value of your stock and debtors minus creditors (as per your monthly stock statement submitted to the bank).

faqs.question: What is CGTMSE?
faqs.answer: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises provides collateral-free loan guarantees for MSME loans up to ₹2 crore. Eligible businesses can get loans without pledging assets.

faqs.question: How long does bank loan processing take?
faqs.answer: For MSME loans up to ₹25 lakh — typically 1–3 weeks. For larger working capital or term loans — 3–8 weeks depending on the bank and documentation completeness.

faqs.question: What is DSCR and why do banks care about it?
faqs.answer: Debt Service Coverage Ratio = Net Operating Income / Total Debt Service. Banks require DSCR > 1.25–1.5x to ensure the business generates enough cash to repay the loan. We calculate and optimise your DSCR before submission.

faqs.question: What is burn rate and runway?
faqs.answer: Burn rate is monthly cash expenditure above revenue. Runway = Cash Balance / Monthly Burn. Investors closely track these — we calculate and present them clearly.

faqs.question: What is contribution margin?
faqs.answer: Contribution Margin = Revenue − Variable Costs. It shows how much each rupee of revenue contributes to covering fixed costs and generating profit. A positive CM is essential before scaling.

faqs.question: How do you identify wasted costs?
faqs.answer: We categorise all expenses, compare against revenue benchmarks, identify duplicate subscriptions, underutilised assets, inefficient processes, and vendor contracts with better alternatives.

faqs.question: What is unit economics?
faqs.answer: Unit economics analyses profitability at the individual unit/transaction level — e.g., profit per order, per customer, or per SKU. Strong unit economics are essential for scaling profitably.

faqs.question: How much can cost optimisation save?
faqs.answer: Typically 5–20% of total operating costs can be reduced without impacting quality or growth, through better vendor terms, process efficiency, and eliminating non-value-adding spends.

faqs.question: When should a business review its pricing?
faqs.answer: At minimum annually, and also when: raw material/input costs change significantly, a new competitor enters, you launch new products, or your margins have been declining for 2+ consecutive quarters.

faqs.question: Why are internal controls important?
faqs.answer: Internal controls prevent fraud, reduce errors, ensure financial reporting accuracy, and demonstrate governance — all critical for investor trust, audits, and regulatory compliance.

faqs.question: What is an SOP in finance?
faqs.answer: A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is a step-by-step document describing how a specific finance process (like vendor payments, expense approvals, or bank reconciliation) should be carried out.

faqs.question: What is a risk register?
faqs.answer: A risk register is a document that lists all identified risks for a business, along with their likelihood, potential impact, current mitigants, and action plans. It's reviewed and updated regularly.

faqs.question: What are the most common internal control weaknesses?
faqs.answer: Common weaknesses: no segregation of duties (same person approves and pays), lack of approval workflows, no surprise cash counts, absence of reconciliations, and missing documentation for transactions.

faqs.question: Is internal control review different from a statutory audit?
faqs.answer: Yes. A statutory audit checks if financial statements are fairly presented. An internal control review assesses the quality and effectiveness of processes and safeguards — it's focused on risk prevention.
